messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'pool-gpu-east-2' at 98% allocation, autoscaler unable to add replicas (quota limit). Queue length rising across models v21.x. See https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/3332100000

alex: seeing large qps increase from rollout_v21. Context median jumped from 1k -> 12k tokens for a subset of clients, kv-cache pressure spiked. Autoscaler hitting hard limit: 'max_replicas=8' per pool.

maria: confirmed. 95th latency is 4.2s and growing. Prefill and streaming backpressure on the hot shard. Customer reports from prod are starting to come in via support.

engops_james: copying current autoscaler logs (truncated):
```
[2026-03-15T18:01:12Z] scale_request -> desired=12, current=8, reason=queue_growth
[2026-03-15T18:01:12Z] scale_decision -> reject, policy_limit=max_replicas(8)
[2026-03-15T18:01:13Z] queue_length=4320, avg_latency=3.8s
```

anna-ml: model rollout v21 included context expansion to support longer conversational state (kv-cache shards expanded). Looks like a subset of clients started sending long-history prompts which multiplied KV entries per request. Not caught by canary because canary traffic mix didn't include those clients.

kt: tagging @sre_lead — can we get a mitigation plan? Customers impacted: a few high-throughput tenants showing 5-10% increased error rates and higher token billing.

sre_lead: escalation acknowledged. Immediate actions in this order: 1) pause v21 rollout and route traffic back to v20 for susceptible routes, 2) apply temporary rate limits for long-context requests, 3) request emergency quota bump from infra for pool-gpu-east-2 (if feasible), 4) open handoff to on-call infra.

alex: executing step 1 — flipping rollout flag now. Command:
```
redwoodctl rollout pause --model v21 --reason "autoscale-limit-queue-spike"
```

alex: paused. Response: "rollout v21 paused, active traffic shifted to v20 for flagged routes" :white_check_mark:

maria: step 2 — implementing adaptive request caps for routes with avg context > 4k. Patch pushed to edge routing: 
```
curl -X POST https://edge.redwood.internal/route-config -d '{"route":"/chat/*","max_context_tokens":4000,"throttle_period_s":30}' -H "Auth: token"
```

maria: applied. Starting to see queue length flattening on hot shard (queue_length down from 4.3k -> 2.1k in 5m). :eyes:

engops_james: opened a request with infra for emergency replica quota: ticket INFRA-2026, pinging vendor for extra nodes. ETA unknown.

anna-ml: quick hotfix we can try: toggle kv-cache-ttl reduction for v21 model instances so cached KV entries expire faster to reclaim memory (temporary). Will need a restart of warmed instances to apply. Impacts latency slightly but may relieve pressure.

kt: do it. We'll accept small latency increase to avoid throttles. Provide command.

anna-ml: running:
```
redwoodctl model-config set --model v21 --kv_cache_ttl 60
redwoodctl pool rolling-restart --pool pool-gpu-east-2 --selector model=v21
```

anna-ml: restart kicked off. Noting prefill spikes during restart, watching closely.

customer-success-sam: notifying largest affected tenants: sending templated note with mitigation status and ask to disable long-history settings if possible.

customer-success-sam: message sent to Tenant A & B: "We're seeing elevated latency for long-context requests. We've paused the recent model rollout and applied throttles to reduce impact. We're actively restoring capacity; we'll follow up once stable."

sre_lead: monitoring metrics. Two things to watch: queue_length and KVCACHE_ENTRIES per instance. If queue_length > 3000 after 15m, escalate to cross-region failover.

alex: queue_length now 1200, avg_latency 2.1s. Error rate trending down. :white_check_mark:

maria: note: a small group of clients send prefills of 50k tokens occasionally; those were rare but now causing disproportionate KV growth. We'll add a hard cap at edge for single-request token limit of 20k until we complete deeper remediation.

kt: agree. Apply global cap and notify dev-integrations.

maria: applied global cap: 
```
edge-config set global_max_tokens=20000
```

engops_james: infra responded: can provision 2 extra GPUs in 90-120m if approved. Approved the emergency quota bump. That will buy headroom for safe rollbacks and gradual re-onboarding.

anna-ml: planning follow-up: 1) add more representative canary tests with long-history clients, 2) add KV-entry accounting to rollout gating, 3) evaluate model quantization config to reduce per-token memory.

sre_lead: handoff plan: on-call to monitor until 02:30 UTC, if metrics stable for 45m we'll close urgent paging. If spikes recur, oncall should trigger cross-region failover procedure and patch routing to dedicated pools.

oncall-bot: Handoff created: incident-3332100000 -> oncall (alex) until 02:30 UTC. Paging suppressed for lower-severity alerts.

alex: leaving final note: root cause appears to be rollout_v21 changing expected context-size distribution. Canary coverage gap + autoscaler policy (hard cap) meant scale couldn't keep up. Immediate mitigations: rollback/pause, edge caps, kv-ttl tweak, emergency quota request. Next steps documented in incident doc: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/3332100000/postmortem

customer-success-sam: follow-up outbound planned in 2 hours with final status & compensation options if error rate materially impacted SLAs.

sre_lead: closing slack thread for active coordination. Will reopen if metrics deviate. :lock:
